summary: The note summarizes plot points from a season of The Office (American TV series). Jim and Pam marry and have a baby, Cecelia Marie Halpert, while Andy and Erin develop mutual interest but struggle to date due to awkwardness. Dunder Mifflin faces bankruptcy rumors and accepts a buyout from Sabre Corporation, a printer company, which lets go Wallace and other executives but spares the Scranton office. The season finale has Dwight buying the office park and Michael Scott negotiating with Sabre CEO Jo Bennet over a press announcement about faulty printers.
one_line: Plot summary of a season of the American TV series The Office, covering the Halperts' marriage, Andy and Erin, and Dunder Mifflin's sale to Sabre.
key_facts: Jim and Pam marry and have a baby named Cecelia Marie Halpert.
Andy and Erin develop mutual interest in one another, but their inherent awkwardness inhibits Andy's attempts to ask Erin out on a date.
Rumors of bankruptcy begin to surround Dunder Mifflin.
By Christmas, Wallace announces to the branch that Dunder Mifflin has accepted a buyout from Sabre Corporation, a printer company.
Wallace and other executives are let go after the Sabre buyout.
The Scranton office survives due to its relative success within the company.
Michael Scott is now the highest level employee at Dunder Mifflin.
In the season finale, Dwight buys the office park.
Michael agrees to make an announcement to the press regarding a case of faulty printers.
Jo Bennet, Sabre CEO, asks how she can repay Michael.
Michael responds that Jo could bring Holly back to the Scranton branch.
